programs.name: last_cycle_replay
programs.description: Use when the latest 24-hour cycle preserves a stable active window but earlier cycle magnitudes are unreliable.
programs.assumption: The next 24 values have lower absolute error when copied from the latest 24-value cycle than when averaged with the preceding cycle; this is falsified if replay loses on subsequent rolling folds.
programs.failure_condition: It fails when pulse timing changes by at least one hour or the next-cycle amplitude changes sharply.

programs.name: scaled_recent_cycle
programs.description: Use when daily pulse timing is stable and total activity changes more smoothly than individual hourly values.
programs.assumption: For two complete 24-value cycles, the next cycle's positive total is within 25% of the latest cycle's total and its active phases match the latest cycle in at least 9 of 11 positions.
programs.failure_condition: It fails when the active window shifts, a new regime starts, or total next-cycle activity differs from the latest cycle by more than 25%.

programs.name: zero_gated_phase_blend
programs.description: Use when inactivity hours are dependable but positive pulse magnitudes benefit from conservative cross-cycle smoothing.
programs.assumption: Hours that are zero in the latest cycle remain zero next cycle with at least 90% accuracy, while a 75/25 latest-to-previous blend reduces positive-hour absolute error versus the parent's stronger historical weighting.
programs.failure_condition: It fails when activity appears in previously inactive phases or when old-cycle values no longer contain useful magnitude information.
